THE COMPLETE PLAYER GUIDE

The rulebook.

Chess V2 keeps the familiar army and adds a hexagonal field, new roles and visible strategic choices. The goal is simple: capture the opposing King.

Learning for the first time?

Open Play → Learn for 16 interactive lessons. Your saved match stays untouched. Follow an objective, ask for a hint, and try the rule on an actual board.

Open the game →
  1. Choose the practice bot or a friend on the same device.
  2. Select Move, a piece, then a legal destination.
  3. Try the other action modes one at a time. Every main action spends a turn.
  4. Capture the King to win. A warning does not restrict your moves.

Download the full rulebook or print a physical set. Both PDFs work without an internet connection.

ALL 17 ROLES

The complete piece set

Every role uses a classical chess pedestal with a distinct silhouette. New crowns include the winged Bee, tiered Hive, shield Warden and spear Lancer. Optional lettered discs use the same codes as the print kit.

Pawn P

One empty hex forward; captures on the two forward flanks. Promotes at the far edge of its file.

Deployment: 2 flux

Knight N

Jumps to 12 destinations. Intervening pieces and walls do not block it; an enemy Anchor does.

Deployment: 3 flux

Bishop B

Slides along six vertex diagonals, staying on one tile color.

Deployment: 3 flux

Rook R

Slides along six edge-connected directions until blocked.

Deployment: 4 flux

Queen Q

Combines Rook and Bishop movement.

Deployment: 6 flux

King K

One adjacent hex. Can be captured. One Royal Exchange with an adjacent unfused Pawn per game.

Never deployed

Warden WA

Warden: Knight jumps plus Rook slides up to two hexes.

Deployment: 5 flux

Archbishop AR

Archbishop: Bishop slides plus Knight jumps.

Deployment: 6 flux

Chancellor CH

Chancellor: Rook slides plus Knight jumps.

Deployment: 7 flux

Bee BE

Bee: flies one or two straight hexes; only adjacent captures. A non-capture allows one other Bee to step.

Deployment: 2 flux

Hive HV

Hive: immobile. Deploy reserve Bees beside it, or split into two Bees with Ability.

Deployment: 4 flux

Hornet HN

Hornet: flies up to three straight hexes; captures only adjacent. No swarm follow-up.

Deployment: 4 flux

Mimic MI

Mimic: borrows movement from adjacent friendly Pawns, Knights, Bishops or Rooks. No neighbor: an empty step only.

Deployment: 4 flux

Anchor AN

Anchor: one adjacent step/capture. Adjacent enemies cannot jump, use gates or fuse.

Deployment: 3 flux

Courier CO

Courier: two empty rook steps, or one while carrying. Ability loads/unloads a friendly unit; never captures.

Deployment: 3 flux

Bastion BA

Bastion: two-hex Rook movement. Adjacent friendly non-Kings are protected from Guard reactions.

Deployment: 4 flux

Lancer LA

Lancer: slides up to three hexes on the three forward axes. Cannot retreat normally.

Deployment: 4 flux

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

01 / The game at a glance

Chess V2 is a chess-rooted strategy game on 127 hexes. Familiar pieces share the field with Bees, support units, fusion forms and a central Nexus. This is the complete rulebook for Chess V2 1.0 (rules edition 3).

Your objective

Capture the opposing King. There is no check or checkmate restriction: an exposed King may remain exposed or move into danger. The red warning is advice, not a prohibition. The game ends immediately when a King is captured.

The field and the armies

The radius-6 hexagonal board has 127 cells. Files run A–M and ranks 1–13; not every file/rank intersection exists. G7 is the Nexus. White moves first; Black follows. Each starts with the familiar 16 chess pieces plus 2 Bees, a Mimic, an Anchor and a Courier: 21 pieces on the field, and a Pawn, Knight and Bee in reserve.

A turn

Take one main action: move, fuse, deploy, build/remove a wall, place/relocate a gate, guard, use a piece ability, use the Nexus, or pass. A non-capturing Bee move may add one optional swarm step before the opponent plays. That step is part of the same turn.

Flux and reserves

Start with 3 flux, capped at 8. A capture grants its captor 1; passing grants 1. A Nexus Harvest grants 3. Unused flux carries over. Captured non-King units return to their own army's reserve. Captured fusions separate into their recorded ingredients. Promoted pawns return as their promoted role.

Draws and omissions

Four consecutive main-turn passes draw; Finish swarm is not a pass. A draw also occurs after 100 quiet main turns. Captures, pawn moves, fusions, deployments, wall/gate changes, split/load/unload/exchange/recall/reforge reset that counter. Guard, Harvest, ordinary non-pawn moves and passes do not. There is no castling, en passant, initial pawn double step, or repetition draw in this edition.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

02 / Familiar pieces, hex movement

Select a piece to reveal exact legal destinations. An empty marker means movement; a ring means capture. Standard pieces capture by landing on an enemy piece. They cannot land on friendly pieces except through a specific ability or fusion.

Rook and Bishop

A Rook slides along the six edge-connected axes until blocked. A Bishop slides along six vertex diagonals, skipping the intermediate cells and staying on one tile color. A piece on its diagonal destination stops the ray; intervening off-ray units do not. Walls can block both types.

Queen and Knight

A Queen combines Rook and Bishop slides. A Knight jumps to 12 possible hexes: two steps along one edge axis and one along its neighboring axis. It ignores intervening pieces and walls, unless adjacent to an enemy Anchor.

King

The King moves and captures one hex along any of six edges. It has no protected status. It can also use its once-per-game Royal Exchange ability described in chapter 6.

Pawn

A Pawn moves one empty hex straight ahead. White moves toward decreasing ranks; Black toward increasing ranks. It captures on the two forward flanks, never straight ahead. For White at G7, the forward move is G6; capture flanks are F7 and H6. Reverse those directions for Black. There is no double step.

Promotion

A Pawn reaching the far edge of its own file promotes immediately to Queen, Rook, Bishop or Knight, chosen in the action dialog. A gate move or guard capture can also promote. A guard-reaction promotion is automatically a Queen. A Mimic copying Pawn movement does not promote.

Coordinates for bot builders

The engine uses axial q,r coordinates with max(abs(q),abs(r),abs(q+r)) <= 6. Display file is q+6, starting at A; display rank is r+7. G7 is 0,0. On the screen, movement previews and the coordinate toggle are the easiest way to learn the geometry.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

03 / Bees and the living army

Bees trade long-distance capture for mobility and coordination. The new units have deliberately different strengths; no special unit replaces the whole chess army.

Bee: flight, sting, swarm

A Bee moves one or two hexes on a straight edge axis. A two-hex flight jumps intervening pieces and walls and must land empty. It captures only on an adjacent hex, respecting the wall on that edge. After a non-capturing Bee move, a different friendly Bee anywhere on the field may step to one adjacent empty hex, without crossing a wall. Select that Bee, then its destination, or press Finish swarm. There is no capture and no chaining on the follow-up. If the first Bee is captured by Guard, no follow-up is awarded.

Hive

Fuse two neighboring Bees into an immobile Hive. It cannot move, capture, guard or travel through gates. It enables reserve Bee deployment on empty adjacent hexes for the normal 2-flux cost and one turn, even outside the home area. It creates no free pieces. Ability mode can split it into two Bees on two distinct empty adjacent hexes for one turn and no flux. Choose the pair in the dialog. Walls do not block emergence or deployment.

Hornet

The alternative Bee+Bee fusion. It flies one to three hexes on an edge axis, with empty landing hexes for longer flights. It captures only adjacent, respecting the edge wall, and never grants a swarm follow-up. An Anchor disables flights of length two or three.

Mimic

The Mimic borrows movement and capture rules from adjacent friendly Pawns, Knights, Bishops and Rooks. If several qualify, it may use any of their moves. It never borrows special abilities or promotion. With no qualifying neighbor, it can step one empty adjacent hex and cannot capture. It cannot Guard. An Anchor still disables its borrowed knight jumps and gate travel.

Anchor

Moves and captures one adjacent hex. An enemy unit adjacent to it cannot use gates, jump, or fuse. This aura crosses walls. Non-jumping movement remains available, so a Bee may still step or sting. A trapped ordinary Knight has no ordinary move until the Anchor is removed or the position changes.

Courier

Moves up to two empty hexes on a Rook axis and never captures. Ability mode loads an adjacent friendly non-King unit, or unloads the passenger onto an adjacent empty hex. Both use a whole turn, cost no flux, and cannot cross a wall. Hives and other Couriers cannot be loaded. A loaded Courier moves only one hex, but may use an unblocked gate to an empty endpoint. Capture sends both Courier and passenger to their owner's reserve. A passenger provides no aura, attacks, or Nexus access while aboard.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

04 / Fusion and new forms

Fuse mode combines two adjacent friendly units on the second unit's hex. It costs 2 flux and the whole turn. No wall may separate them, neither may be anchored or carry a passenger, and Kings never fuse. Where two results are offered, choose one in the dialog.

The recipes

Pawn + Pawn = Knight. Knight + Pawn = Warden. Bishop + Knight = Archbishop OR Mimic. Rook + Knight = Chancellor. Rook + Bishop = Queen. Bee + Bee = Hive OR Hornet. Rook + Pawn = Bastion OR Lancer.

Warden, Archbishop, Chancellor

A Warden combines Knight jumps with Rook slides of at most two hexes. An Archbishop combines Bishop slides with Knight jumps. A Chancellor combines Rook slides with Knight jumps. Enemy Anchors disable the jumping component, but leave legal sliding moves available.

Bastion

A Bastion moves and captures like a Rook limited to two hexes. It shields adjacent friendly non-King units from automatic Guard captures. Ordinary captures still work, and the Bastion itself is not protected by its own aura. Its shield crosses walls. The King can never receive this protection.

Lancer

A Lancer moves and captures up to three hexes on three forward edge axes. For White these are the Pawn's forward direction and both capture flanks; Black uses the reverse. It cannot retreat through ordinary movement. Like other mobile units it may use a gate, unless anchored.

Ingredients and recovery

A fusion remembers its components. If captured or recalled, those components return separately to the owner's reserve. A Pawn+Pawn Knight can later fuse with another Pawn into a Warden; its recorded components are then three Pawns. Only two-component fusions qualify for Nexus Reforge in this edition.

Reforge

While one of your units occupies G7, use Nexus mode to select a friendly two-component fusion anywhere on the field and choose another result from the same recipe. The unit stays on its hex; the action costs a turn and no flux. Only Bee+Bee, Bishop+Knight and Rook+Pawn currently offer alternate forms. Anchored units cannot reforge.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

05 / The battlefield is a resource

Construction is never forbidden by a threatened King. It can be a useful answer to a threat, but the King still falls if the opponent captures it next.

Walls

Each army may have two wall segments, each on a boundary between neighboring hexes. Build for 1 flux; remove your own for no flux. Either uses a turn. You cannot remove enemy walls. Relocation takes two separate turns: remove, then build. Walls block both armies equally.

Corners and jumps

An adjacent move cannot cross its wall. For a Bishop-style diagonal step, any wall along either of the two short edge routes around the crossed vertex blocks the step, symmetrically in both directions. Knight jumps and longer Bee/Hornet flights ignore walls. Anchors disable those jumps or flights. A flying piece must still have a valid landing hex.

Gates

Each army may build one pair. An endpoint costs 2 flux and a turn. Place on an empty hex in your half: White ranks 8–13; Black ranks 1–6. G7 is excluded. Endpoints cannot overlap any gate or touch their paired endpoint. Relocate an endpoint for 2 flux only when its old hex is empty.

Shared travel

After both endpoints exist, either army may use the pair. A piece already on an endpoint can spend its move travelling to the other, capturing an enemy there if its role permits capture. Entering and travelling are separate moves. The gate capture is an exception to Bee/Hornet sting range. Couriers can travel only to empty endpoints; Hives cannot travel. An adjacent enemy Anchor blocks departure.

The Nexus: G7

Occupancy, not permanent ownership, grants access. There is no automatic claim bonus or passive income. While one of your units occupies G7, choose one whole-turn action: Harvest +3 flux; Recall one friendly non-King unit to its reserve; or Reforge a qualifying fusion. The occupant may recall itself, which gives up Nexus access. Recall splits fusion ingredients; a recalled Courier also returns its passenger's ingredients. Walls do not block remote Recall or Reforge.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

06 / Guard and Royal Exchange

These rules change how you plan a turn. The game always shows guard targets, and King danger remains advisory.

Set a guard

Guard mode lets a piece mark one hex it could currently capture, including an empty hex. The action spends a turn and costs no flux. Each army has at most one guard; setting a new one replaces the old. A guard lasts through the opponent's turn, including an optional swarm step, and expires when its owner's next turn begins. Hives, Couriers and Mimics cannot Guard.

The reaction

When an enemy arrives on the marked hex, the guard automatically captures it if the guarding unit still exists and could legally capture that hex at that moment. The guarding unit moves onto the target; the token is consumed; the captor gains 1 flux. If the attack is blocked, or a Bastion protects the arriving non-King unit, no reaction occurs. Guard reactions do not trigger further guard reactions or swarm moves.

Which arrivals trigger it?

Ordinary moves, gate travel, swarm steps, reserve deployment, fusion, Hive split, Courier unloading and Royal Exchange can trigger a guard. Recall and loading remove a piece and do not trigger it. Reforge changes a piece in place and does not trigger it. During a Hive split, the first listed destination resolves before the second. In Royal Exchange, the King's destination resolves first.

King capture takes priority

If the main move already captures a King, the game ends immediately: no subsequent guard or secondary effect can reverse that win. A guard itself can capture a King and win. Reaction pawn promotions become Queens automatically.

Royal Exchange

Once per army per game, the King may swap places with an adjacent friendly, unfused Pawn. Use Ability mode, select the King, then the highlighted Pawn. The edge must be free of walls. It costs a full turn and no flux. It grants no invulnerability; the King's destination can trigger Guard, and it remains capturable afterward.

Useful interaction

A Rook can guard the far endpoint of a gate. The opponent can remove the Rook, block its line, protect the arriving non-King piece with a Bastion, or avoid that endpoint. All threats are public; there are no hidden cards, rolls or random combat outcomes.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

07 / Your first match

Choose Learn to enter 16 interactive lessons. Each lesson uses a separate position, checks your action and offers a hint. Your live match is restored on exit. You can also use the steps below in local two-player mode.

1. Read the field

The board uses white and black pieces, three neutral tile shades, and a small Nexus marker at G7. Click a piece and a destination, or use the arrow keys and Enter on the board. Zoom enlarges the cells; the board then scrolls. Flip reverses the view without renaming coordinates. All tokens replaces every silhouette with its printable code.

2. Try a Bee

For a controlled lesson, choose Friend · on this device. Select Move, then White's Bee at C10, then the empty C9. The turn remains White's for an optional swarm step. Select the other Bee at D10 and move to empty E9, or press Finish swarm. Black then plays.

3. Try fusion in a fresh match

Choose Friend · on this device, Fuse, C10, then D10. Select Hive or Hornet in the dialog. This costs 2 of White's starting 3 flux. After the opponent acts, use Ability on a Hive to choose two empty emergence hexes. Alternatively, save flux and use a reserve Bee beside the Hive.

4. Bring a reserve piece back

Click a reserve card below the board, then an empty highlighted home hex. Starting examples include A13 and G13 for White. Bees may also deploy beside a friendly Hive. A disabled card means insufficient flux, no valid destination, or a bot is currently acting.

5. Learn the rest gradually

Use Guard to see the public target ring. Use Ability for Courier load/unload, Hive split and Royal Exchange. Use Nexus while occupying G7 for Harvest, Recall or Reforge. The field manual explains exact movement and recipes. Undo is available for experimentation.

6. Watch and test

Watch bots play runs both armies. Pause stops pending search. One bot action advances a single engine action; Bee movement and its optional swarm decision are separate actions in one turn. The test runner is under Save, load & test. It uses isolated states and reports the turn cap as unfinished. Undo takes back one action and pauses bots.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

08 / Quick reference and bot interface

Chess V2 rules rules are deterministic. Bots use the same legal actions as people. Their move selection varies with a seed; movement and combat themselves do not use chance.

Flux costs

Move, Guard, Load, Unload, Split, Royal Exchange, Recall and Reforge: 0. Fuse: 2. Build wall: 1. Remove own wall: 0. Gate placement or relocation: 2. Pass: gain 1. Harvest: gain 3. Each capture: gain 1. Every main action costs one turn, even if its flux cost is zero.

Deployment costs

Pawn 2; Bee 2; Knight 3; Bishop 3; Anchor 3; Courier 3; Rook 4; Hornet 4; Hive 4; Mimic 4; Bastion 4; Lancer 4; Warden 5; Queen 6; Archbishop 6; Chancellor 7. Kings cannot deploy. In normal play, captured fusion forms split into ingredients rather than entering reserve as a form.

Choose the right mode

Move: normal movement or a swarm follow-up. Fuse: combine friendly neighbors. Deploy: reserve to board. Wall/Gate: construction. Ability: Hive, Courier or King actions. Guard: set a reaction target. Nexus: Harvest, Recall or Reforge. Multiple outcomes open an explicit choice dialog.

Bot access

The Bot interface exports an observation. window.ChessV2.getObservation() returns version, revision, state and legalActions. Submit a listed ID with window.ChessV2.submitAction(id, revision). Use local mode and pause autoplay for an external bot. Tutorial mode rejects external actions. Illegal actions and stale revisions are rejected.

Compatibility and limits

Ordinary UCI chess engines do not understand this board or its rules. They require a custom adapter and variant implementation. The bundled bot is a heuristic practice opponent: Tactical uses an eight-candidate beam and does not consider construction in opponent replies. The engine and protocol documentation are included with the game. No online multiplayer is implemented.

Version and testing

Chess V2 1.0 retains Swarm rules edition 3. The site runs entirely in the browser. Download match exports a replayable save; Load match validates each action before replacing the current game. Tutorials use separate positions and preserve your live game. Competitive balance remains experimental.

CHESS V2 / RULES EDITION 3

09 / Play on a real table

The digital and physical games use the same rules. Use a normal chess set for the familiar pieces and the provided lettered discs for special roles, or print an entirely flat token set. No electronic device is needed for play.

Print and assemble

The Print-and-Play PDF contains a one-sheet A3 board, four A4 board tiles, separate White and Black token sheets, markers, and a tracking sheet. Choose the A3 board OR assemble the four A4 tiles at 100% scale. Cut on the square guides and join matching top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right edges. The assembled A4 board is 360 x 360 mm. Check the 50 mm scale line before cutting.

Set up the armies

Use the setup table on the tracking sheet. Each army has 21 on-board units plus Pawn, Knight and Bee in reserve. White starts with 3 flux, Black with 3. Put the Nexus marker on G7. Begin with no walls or gates, no guards, and each Royal Exchange marker available.

The same piece codes

P Pawn; N Knight; B Bishop; R Rook; Q Queen; K King. BE Bee; HV Hive; HN Hornet; MI Mimic; AN Anchor; CO Courier. WA Warden; AR Archbishop; CH Chancellor; BA Bastion; LA Lancer. Black and white discs identify ownership. Blank discs are spares: write any code on them when a promotion or fusion needs another token.

Track ingredients and passengers

Give every fused unit a small ID, such as W1 or B1. Record its original ingredients on the tracking sheet and update its square when it moves. On capture or Recall, return those ingredients to its owner’s reserve. For a loaded Courier, place the passenger beside its tracking entry, not on the board. A passenger has no attacks or aura.

Track turns and reactions

Mark flux from 0 to 8. Place a Guard token on the target and record its guarding piece’s square; remove it when its owner’s turn begins or its reaction fires. Mark Royal Exchange as used after swapping. If a Bee earns a swarm step, keep the turn marker on its owner until the step is made or declined. Track consecutive passes and the quiet-turn counter for draws.

Construction and disputes

Use two wall strips per army and two numbered gate markers per army. Place walls on edges, never inside hexes. Gates sit under pieces so occupancy remains clear. Use the full rulebook for corner blocking, Anchor effects and reaction order. All information is public; if a position becomes ambiguous, stop and reconstruct it from the move log.

About this edition

Concept and game design by Mahdi Hazrati (مهدی حضرتی). Website release 1.2.0. Rules edition 3, unchanged from the Swarm variant. This is a static application with no accounts, trackers, ads or server. Match data and learning progress stay in your browser. A downloaded match can be imported and is validated move by move.

The built-in bot is a practice opponent, not a professional chess engine. Tactical search uses a limited two-ply beam. Competitive balance has not been established. No online multiplayer, ratings, chess clock or cloud sync is included.

For developers, see the included README and bot protocol. The GitHub Pages deployment works from a repository subpath without changing links or worker URLs.
